checks: Compiled source mutant rejected by exact boundary test
Current typed relations and corresponding focused Rust tests are listed in adjacent model.md and model.md#evidence.
cost: O(n) byte comparisons and O(n) output words, O(1) auxiliary words. Successful uncached comparisons advance the nondecreasing right boundary; each center contributes at most one unsuccessful comparison. No throughput measurement.
forward: For a byte sequence s of length n, return n lengths. z[0]=n when n>0; for i>0 z[i]=max{k<=n-i: s[0..k]=s[i..i+k]}. Empty input returns [].
inverse: Universe: finite byte inputs paired with arbitrary usize vectors. Excluded outputs have incorrect length, z[0] != n when n>0, a radius beyond the suffix, an unequal byte inside a claimed match, or an extendable nonmaximal radius. This mathematical exclusion relation is not replaced by negative tests.

Given vector v, compatible antecedents are all byte strings s with length n=v.len(), 0<=v[i]<=n-i for every index i, v[0]=n when nonempty, equalities s[j]=s[i+j] for j<v[i], and inequality s[v[i]]!=s[i+v[i]] whenever i+v[i]<n. Empty vector admits only empty input. Constraints can be inconsistent; symbol names are not recoverable uniquely.
limitations: Partial syntax; finite tests do not prove all inputs; byte rather than Unicode character semantics.
state: All finite byte slices and returned usize vector observations.
